take_homes: Closing a door on the agent is the cheapest control, and it costs a feature. Someone has to sign for that trade-off.
Agent checks sit on top of our normal controls and do not replace them. One test run proves little because the agent answers differently each time.
The audit report sorts rules into compliant, violating and can't tell. The can't-tell rows go to legal or IT with the report and one narrow question.

monday.move: Ask IT security whether the agent tool is approved for finance data, and what they would need to see. Bring the policy lens report if I have one. Then ask my controller to try the variance commentary once.
monday.who: IT security lead, then my controller
monday.when: Monday morning for IT; the controller task only after IT replies
monday.stop_condition: IT says no or gives no answer within two weeks, or the controller needs more than an hour to set it up.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: The packaged check carries our own judgment about what matters in our system. That is something we build, not a licence we buy. I still have no cost or payback figure, so it is only shaken.

one_line: Good on what you give up when you limit an agent, but forty minutes of chatting with a bot, repeated filler, and no euro figure anywhere.
